newsitem.title: USA: US Coast Guard calls off search for helicopter crew.
newsitem.headline: US Coast Guard calls off search for helicopter crew.

text.p: A search was called off Thursday for four crew members of a Coast Guard helicopter that crashed during a rescue mission off the northern California coast, officials said.

Coast Guard cutters and aircraft searched around the clock for four days, covering 27,000 square-miles. The Coast Guard suspended the search because there was little chance of finding survivors, Petty Officer Paul Rhynard said.

The Coast Guard helicopter went down late Sunday night after responding to a distress call from a Canadian vessel 57 miles (100 km) west of Cape Mendocino, about 200 miles (320 km) north of San Francisco. At the time, the seas were rough, with waves 26 feet high and winds gusting from 35 to 55 knots.

The four missing helicopter crew members were identified as: Lt. Jeffery Crane from Massachusetts, Lt. Charles Thigpen from California, Petty Officer Richard Hughes from Arizona and Petty Officer James Caines from Georgia.
The five people aboard the Canadian sailboat, the Ezra II, were rescued in good condition by a Coast Guard cutter that was dispatched along with the missing helicopter.
